algorithm_name: SD-Temper — Signed-Discrimination Tempering for self-consistency voting (working name in the seed: "RTC"; renamed to avoid the ReASC / "reliability-aware" collision, arXiv 2601.02970). Two variants: SD-Temper-Dev (small labeled dev split, primary) and SD-Temper-LF (label-free / online, secondary).
summary: SD-Temper turns "how much should I trust this model's confidence channel?" into one scalar estimand — the signed within-item discrimination D (stratified Somers' D = 2*WQD-1, a pure rank statistic, hence invariant to any monotone miscalibration) — estimates it with an item-clustered confidence interval, soft-thresholds it at the CI radius (so no evidence => exactly zero trust), and pushes the shrunk value through a closed-form Gaussian-log-likelihood-ratio map g to the exponent of an exponential-family vote weight w_i = exp(gamma * s_i). The weight family contains plain SC (gamma=0, exactly) and CISC (score map psi=identity, gamma=1/T, bit-for-bit) as exact members, so the two anchor points of G4 are algebraic identities, not limits. Because D is signed, an anti-correlated channel (kappa_c<0) yields gamma<0 and is *exploited* rather than merely survived; because the trust magnitude is the CI lower bound rather than the point estimate, estimator noise near D=0 collapses to SC by construction (P(gamma_hat != 0 | D=0) <= 2*alpha). The label-free variant reuses the identical functional with agreement-with-plurality as a noisy correctness label, initialized by a margin-weighted moment estimator and refined by a Raykar-style latent-truth EM whose first iteration *is* the agreement proxy; its poisoning under echo/correlated errors is quantified exactly (D_agr = (1-eps)*D + eps*E) and its sign is provably unidentifiable without labels or an extra elicitation channel, so the honest deployment default is "magnitude label-free, sign certified on a tiny dev split". Positioning is deliberately modest: WQD (discrimination-not-calibration) is CISC's own metric, rank-power voting is self-certainty Borda's, shrinkage is James-Stein/SafeBayes, the EM is Raykar 2010. The contributions are (i) the signed, shrunk, anchored composition, (ii) the adversarial confidence-usage frontier (D<0), and (iii) the pre-registered falsifier discipline including the reparametrization of the simulator's kappa_c axis onto the estimand D, which reveals that the existing sweep contains no genuinely weak-signal point.
emphasis: Dev-calibrated first. The statistical core is: (1) the functional is stratified (within-item) Somers' D = 2*AUC-1 = 2*WQD-1, computed by the Mann-Whitney rank-sum identity, pooled across items with pair-count weights; (2) its uncertainty must be computed with the ITEM as the independent sampling unit (traces within an item are dependent) — cluster-sandwich or item-level BCa bootstrap, never a pooled-pairs DeLong; (3) the trust magnitude used downstream is the Fisher-z soft-thresholded value tanh(S_lambda(atanh D_hat)) with lambda = t_{1-alpha,Qeff-1} * SE_zeta — i.e. the CI *lower* bound, continuous, odd, and exactly zero when the CI covers zero; (4) the map from reliability to exponent is derived (Gaussian LLR slope on the rank-normalized scale), not grid-searched, precisely so SD-Temper-Dev is not just a re-run of CISC's published dev-tuned-temperature protocol. The label-free variant is a bonus built on the same functional with agreement-as-noisy-label, and its limits are stated as theorems-of-impossibility, not engineering gaps.
math:
## 0. Notation and data model

Items q = 1..Q (iid). Item q has m_q cached traces; trace i carries answer a_{qi}, confidence c_{qi} in [0,1], generated tokens g_{qi}, and pairwise semantic/duplicate similarity Sim_q[i,j] (all present in TracePool). Answers are mapped to equivalence classes ("answer clusters") by the harness's existing dedup: cl(a_{qi}) in {1..K_q}. n_{qa} = #{i : cl(a_{qi}) = a}. Gold cluster a*_q known only on the dev split. Per-trace correctness x_{qi} = 1[cl(a_{qi}) = a*_q].

## 1. The weight family (one line, contains SC and CISC)

Score map psi : [0,1]^{m_q} -> R^{m_q} (may be within-item). Vote weight and aggregator:

    s_q = psi(c_q)
    w_{qi}(gamma) = exp(gamma * s_{qi})
    S_q(a; gamma) = sum_{i : cl(a_{qi}) = a} w_{qi}(gamma)
    a_hat_q(gamma) = argmax_a S_q(a; gamma)      [deterministic tie-break: highest n_{qa}, then lowest cluster id]

Score maps:
  psi_raw(c)_i  = c_i                                            (CISC-softmax anchor mode)
  psi_log(c)_i  = log max(c_i, 1e-6)                             (CISC-power anchor mode, w = c^gamma)
  psi_rank(c)_i = STANDARDIZED BLOM NORMAL SCORES  (DEFAULT):
        r_i  = midrank of c_i within item q (ties -> average rank), r_i in [1, m_q]
        u_i  = (r_i - 0.375) / (m_q + 0.25)
        v_i  = Phi^{-1}(u_i)
        s_i  = (v_i - mean(v)) / sd(v)   if sd(v) > 1e-12, else s_i = 0 for all i
  psi_unif(c)_i = standardized (u_i - 1/2)                        (ablation)

psi_rank is invariant to every strictly increasing transform of c (it is a function of ranks only) and is *by construction* mean-0/unit-variance within each item, which is exactly the scale the tempering map in §4 assumes. The all-ties fallback s == 0 makes the method degenerate to SC on tie-degenerate items — the desired safe behaviour for lumpy verbalized confidences.

Numerical form actually implemented: w = exp(gamma*s - max_i(gamma*s_i)) (argmax-invariant, overflow-free).

## 2. The reliability functional: signed within-item discrimination

### 2.1 Per-item statistic (Mann-Whitney / WQD)
For item q let n_q^+ = sum_i x_{qi}, n_q^- = m_q - n_q^+. Item q is INFORMATIVE iff n_q^+ n_q^- > 0. For informative q, with R_q^+ = sum of midranks of c over the correct traces:

    U_hat_q = ( R_q^+ - n_q^+ (n_q^+ + 1)/2 ) / ( n_q^+ n_q^- )        (1)
    d_hat_q = 2 U_hat_q - 1   in [-1, 1]                                (2)

(1) is algebraically identical to the pairwise definition
U_hat_q = (n_q^+ n_q^-)^{-1} * sum_{i:x=1} sum_{j:x=0} [1(c_i > c_j) + 0.5*1(c_i = c_j)],
i.e. exactly CISC's Within-Question Discrimination, and costs O(m log m) rather than O(m^2). d_hat_q is the rank-biserial correlation / Somers' D_{c|x}.

### 2.2 Pooling across items
    omega_q = n_q^+ n_q^-                                (default: pair-count = pooled WQD)
    omega_q = n_q^+ n_q^- / (m_q + 1)                    (option: van Elteren optimal-variance)
    Q_eff = #{informative items}
    D_hat = ( sum_q omega_q d_hat_q ) / ( sum_q omega_q )                (3)

### 2.3 Sampling distribution (exact statements)
(a) Conditional on (n_q^+, n_q^-), U_hat_q is an UNBIASED estimator of U_q = P(c_correct > c_incorrect) + 0.5 P(tie), with exact Hanley-McNeil variance
    Var(U_hat_q) = [ U(1-U) + (n^+ -1)(Q1 - U^2) + (n^- -1)(Q2 - U^2) ] / (n^+ n^-),
    Q1 = P(two correct both exceed one incorrect), Q2 = P(one correct exceeds two incorrect);
    exponential approximation Q1 = U/(2-U), Q2 = 2U^2/(1+U).
This is reported as a diagnostic ONLY. It must NOT be used for the CI, because traces inside an item are dependent and items, not pairs, are the iid unit.

(b) D_hat in (3) is a ratio estimator over iid items => consistent, with O(1/Q_eff) ratio bias. Its correct (cluster-robust, item-level sandwich) variance is

    Var_hat(D_hat) = [ Q_eff / (Q_eff - 1) ] * sum_q omega_q^2 (d_hat_q - D_hat)^2 / ( sum_q omega_q )^2      (4)

which equals the delete-one-ITEM jackknife of (3) to first order. (4) automatically absorbs the within-item variance of U_hat_q because d_hat_q carries it.

(c) Variance-stabilize with Fisher z (delta method, dzeta/dD = 1/(1-D^2)):
    zeta_hat = atanh( clip(D_hat, -1+1e-6, 1-1e-6) )
    SE_zeta  = sqrt( Var_hat(D_hat) ) / (1 - D_hat^2)                                  (5)
    sqrt(Q_eff) (zeta_hat - zeta) -> N(0, sigma_zeta^2); use t_{Q_eff - 1} quantiles at finite Q_eff.

(d) SMALL-n DEFAULT: when Q_eff <= 200, replace (4)-(5) by an ITEM-LEVEL (cluster) BCa bootstrap with B = 2000 resamples of items (resample items with replacement, recompute (3)); take lambda from the BCa interval endpoints on the zeta scale. Sandwich+t is used when Q_eff > 200. Both are exposed; the bootstrap is the pre-registered default for the dev variant at n_dev in [50,200].

(e) ESTIMAND CAVEAT (state in the paper): dropping non-informative items means D estimates discrimination *conditional on the item having both a correct and an incorrect trace*. The per-trace accuracy p_bar used in §4 is computed over ALL dev traces, informative or not.

(f) Design formula: SE(D_hat) ~= sd_q(d_hat_q) / sqrt(Q_eff). Empirically sd_q(d_hat_q) in [0.25, 0.55] at m=40, so SE ~= 0.4/sqrt(Q_eff): Q_eff=50 -> 0.057, Q_eff=100 -> 0.040, Q_eff=200 -> 0.028. The soft-threshold radius (§3) is ~1.7*SE, so the minimum detectable |D| that earns any trust is ~0.10 at n_dev=100. Pre-register this.

## 3. Shrinkage: from D_hat to signed trust rho_hat (the CI-lower-bound rule)

Let S_lambda(x) = sign(x) * max(0, |x| - lambda) (soft threshold). With lambda = t_{1-alpha, Q_eff-1} * SE_zeta (or the BCa half-width on the zeta scale):

    rho_hat = tanh( S_lambda( atanh D_hat ) )                                          (6)

Equivalently: rho_hat = D_LCB if D_LCB > 0; D_UCB if D_UCB < 0; 0 otherwise, where [D_LCB, D_UCB] = tanh(zeta_hat -/+ lambda). Properties (proved in anchor_proofs): continuous in (D_hat, lambda), odd in D_hat, non-decreasing in D_hat, non-increasing in lambda, and rho_hat = 0 exactly on |atanh D_hat| <= lambda — a positive-measure event, so SC is ATTAINED, not approached. False-trust rate: P(rho_hat != 0 | D = 0) <= 2*alpha.

Optional EB alternative (reported, not default): positive-part James-Stein on the z scale,
    zeta_EB = zeta_hat * max(0, 1 - SE_zeta^2 / zeta_hat^2),  rho_hat = tanh(zeta_EB).

## 4. Tempering map g: rho_hat -> gamma_hat (derived, not grid-searched)

Model on the rank-normalized scale (exact under psi_rank, which forces the within-item pooled score to be ~N(0,1)): within item q, s | correct ~ N(mu_+, tau^2), s | incorrect ~ N(mu_-, tau^2), mixing weight p = P(correct). Rank normalization pins the pooled moments: mean 0, variance 1. Writing Delta = mu_+ - mu_-, mu_+ = (1-p)Delta, mu_- = -p*Delta, and

    1 = tau^2 + p(1-p) Delta^2.                                                         (7)

The within-item AUC is scale-free: U = Phi( Delta / (tau*sqrt(2)) ), so with kappa := Delta/tau,

    kappa(rho) = sqrt(2) * Phi^{-1}( (1 + rho)/2 ).                                     (8)

The per-trace log-likelihood ratio for "this trace is correct" is exactly linear:
    log [ N(s; mu_+, tau^2) / N(s; mu_-, tau^2) ] = (Delta/tau^2) s + (mu_-^2 - mu_+^2)/(2 tau^2)
                                                  = gamma_LLR * s + beta_off,
    gamma_LLR = Delta / tau^2 = kappa / tau,     beta_off = kappa^2 (2p - 1)/2.
From (7), tau^2 = 1/(1 + p(1-p) kappa^2), hence the closed-form map

    g(rho; p_bar) = kappa(rho) * sqrt( 1 + p_bar (1 - p_bar) kappa(rho)^2 )             (9)
    gamma_hat = clip( g(rho_hat; p_bar), -gamma_max, +gamma_max ),  gamma_max = 4.0     (10)

with p_bar = mean per-trace accuracy on dev (label-free: mean posterior correctness from EM, §6). Setting variance_correction=false gives the simpler g(rho) = kappa(rho); the correction factor lies in [1, sqrt(1 + kappa^2/4)] and is <= 1.12 for |kappa| <= 1.

Honest statement of the aggregation-form gap (must appear in the paper): under conditional independence the EXACT Bayes aggregator is ADDITIVE in log-odds,
    S_q^{logpool}(a) = beta_0 * n_{qa} + gamma_hat * sum_{i : cl(a_{qi}) = a} s_{qi},   beta_0 = logit(p_bar) + kappa^2(2 p_bar - 1)/2,
whereas the CISC-compatible family of §1 is MULTIPLICATIVE. They agree to first order: exp(gamma s) = 1 + gamma s + O(gamma^2), so S_q(a; gamma) = n_{qa} + gamma*sum_{i in a} s_{qi} + O(gamma^2), which is S_q^{logpool} rescaled by 1/beta_0. We keep the multiplicative form as DEFAULT because only it satisfies the exact CISC anchor (G4); LOGPOOL is shipped as ablation A9 with the same gamma_hat and its own SC anchor (gamma=0 => argmax n_{qa}, valid whenever beta_0 > 0).

## 5. SD-Temper-Dev (primary variant) — full estimator

Input: dev pool D_dev (n_dev items with gold), test pool.
  1. For each dev item: s_q = psi_rank(c_q); x_{qi} = 1[cl(a_{qi}) = a*_q]; if informative, compute (U_hat_q, omega_q) via (1)-(2).
  2. If Q_eff < Q_min (default 20): gamma_hat = 0 (= SC). Emit a warning.
  3. D_hat, Var_hat, zeta_hat, SE_zeta by (3)-(5) or BCa; lambda = t_{1-alpha,Q_eff-1} * SE_zeta.
  4. rho_hat by (6); p_bar = mean_{all dev traces} x; gamma_hat by (8)-(10).
  5. Test time: for each test item, s = psi_rank(c), predict argmax_a sum_{i in a} exp(gamma_hat * s_i).
Cross-fitting (for reporting dev-set accuracy without optimism): 5-fold, gamma_hat fitted on 4 folds, applied to the 5th. Test-set numbers need no cross-fitting (dev and test are disjoint).

## 6. SD-Temper-LF (label-free / online) — same functional, noisy label

Replace correctness x by AGREEMENT with the unweighted plurality:
    a_hat_q = argmax_a n_{qa},   pi_q = n_{q,a_hat_q} / m_q,   y_{qi} = 1[cl(a_{qi}) = a_hat_q].

### 6.1 Exact poisoning identity (the quantification the seed asks for)
Let e_q = 1[a_hat_q correct]. If e_q = 1 then y_{qi} = x_{qi} for every i, hence d^{agr}_q = d_q exactly. If e_q = 0, the agreeing set is entirely incorrect and the correct traces sit in the disagreeing set, so d^{agr}_q measures discrimination of confidence for ECHO-CLUSTER MEMBERSHIP; call it E_q. Therefore, with eps := (sum_q omega_q (1-e_q)) / (sum_q omega_q) the omega-weighted echo rate,

    D^{agr} = (1 - eps) * D + eps * E,      bias = eps * (E - D).                      (11)

Special cases: (i) "mirror echo" (the wrong cluster's confidence behaves like the correct cluster's), E = -D, gives the class-conditional-noise attenuation D^{agr} = (1-2 eps) D — SIGN PRESERVED for eps < 1/2, de-attenuable by D_hat = D_hat^{agr}/(1 - 2 eps_hat). (ii) "high-confidence echo" (E > 0 while D <= 0), the sign flips once eps*E > (1-eps)*|D|, i.e. at eps* = |D| / (|D| + E). With D = -0.5 and E = +0.8, eps* = 0.385: a 39% echo rate is enough to make the label-free estimator confidently wrong-signed. Report eps* per regime.

### 6.2 Mitigations (all specified, all ablatable)
  M1 Margin weighting / restriction: keep items with pi_q >= pi_min (default 0.5) and use omega_q^{lf} = omega_q * max(0, 2*pi_q - 1). Rationale: eps is decreasing in pi_q.
  M2 De-attenuation: eps_hat from an isotonic fit of e_q on pi_q on dev (semi-label-free) or from a fixed prior; D_hat <- clip(D_hat^{agr} / (1 - 2*eps_hat), -1, 1). OFF by default (it amplifies bias when (11) case (ii) holds); reported as ablation.
  M3 Echo/dependence diagnostic (uses TracePool similarity): effective independent trace count
        n_eff_q = m_q^2 / sum_{i,j} Sim_q[i,j].
     Flag item q echo-suspect if n_eff_q / m_q < dup_min (default 0.5) OR if the plurality cluster's mean intra-similarity exceeds the mean cross-cluster similarity by more than delta_dup (default 0.15). Drop flagged items from the estimator; if the flagged fraction exceeds phi_max (default 0.3), multiply gamma_hat by a global damping factor (1 - flagged_fraction) and log a WARN.
  M4 Sign certification (recommended deployment default; makes the variant semi-label-free): take |gamma_hat| from the label-free estimator and sign(gamma_hat) from a tiny labeled set (n_sign >= 25 informative items suffices: the sign test on d_hat_q has power > 0.9 at |D| >= 0.3, n=25).
  M5 No self-leakage: when predicting item q, use gamma_hat computed from the window EXCLUDING q (leave-one-item-out in batch; in the online setting, from strictly earlier items only).

### 6.3 Raykar-style latent-truth EM (stage 2; the agreement proxy is its first iteration)
Init: gamma^{(0)} from §6.2 stage 1; beta_0^{(0)} = logit(p_bar^{(0)}), p_bar^{(0)} = mean_q pi_q.
Repeat t = 1..T (default 20) or until |gamma^{(t)} - gamma^{(t-1)}| < 1e-3:
  E-step:  post_q(a) = softmax_a [ beta_0 * n_{qa} + gamma * sum_{i : cl(a_{qi})=a} s_{qi} ];  t_{qi} = post_q( cl(a_{qi}) ).
  M-step:  soft stratified Somers' D with weights t (correct) x (1-t) (incorrect):
              U^{soft}_q = sum_{i,j} t_{qi}(1-t_{qj})[1(c_i>c_j) + 0.5*1(c_i=c_j)] / sum_{i,j} t_{qi}(1-t_{qj}),
              omega^{soft}_q = sum_{i,j} t_{qi}(1-t_{qj}) * max(0, 2 pi_q - 1);
           pool by (3), shrink by (6) with the SAME cluster bootstrap/sandwich, p_bar <- mean_{q,i} t_{qi},
           gamma_raw <- g(rho_hat; p_bar);  gamma <- clip(gamma_raw, gamma^{(0)} - Delta_max, gamma^{(0)} + Delta_max)   [trust region, Delta_max = 1.0];
           beta_0 <- logit(p_bar) + kappa(rho_hat)^2 (2 p_bar - 1)/2.
Structural note worth stating: at gamma = 0, beta_0 > 0, the E-step posterior is the hard plurality, so ONE EM iteration reproduces the agreement proxy exactly; EM is a strict refinement, and its runaway failure mode (self-confirming echo) is exactly why the trust region and M3 exist.
U^{soft}_q is computed in O(m log m) by sorting c and running prefix sums of t and (1-t) over tie groups — never O(m^2).

### 6.4 Online schedule
Burn-in: first B = 50 items use gamma = 0 (pure SC). Thereafter refresh gamma_hat every K = 25 items from a sliding window of the most recent W = 400 items (or all history), excluding the current item. Emit (D_hat, SE, rho_hat, gamma_hat, flagged_fraction) per refresh for auditing.

## 7. Complexity and memory
Per item: sort O(m log m); rank-sum AUC O(m log m); weights and vote O(m + K). Dev fit: O(Q m log m) plus B=2000 cluster-bootstrap resamples of the CACHED per-item (d_hat_q, omega_q) pairs, i.e. O(B*Q) = O(8e5) flops — milliseconds. EM: T * O(Q m log m). Similarity diagnostic: O(m^2) per item only if Sim is materialized (it already is in TracePool); otherwise skip M3. Memory O(Q m). Everything vectorizes over the (Q, m) array; scipy.stats.rankdata(axis=1), scipy.stats.norm.ppf, np.bincount for the cluster sums.

## 8. Reparametrization of the harness sweep (important, checkable)
The simulator's confidence model c_i = clip(0.5 + kappa_c (x_i - 0.5) + N(0, sigma), 0.01, 0.99) with sigma = 0.1 implies, before clipping, that correct/incorrect confidences are Gaussians separated by kappa_c with common sd sigma. Hence the estimand is

    D(kappa_c, sigma) = 2 * Phi( kappa_c / (sigma * sqrt(2)) ) - 1,                     (12)
    inverse: kappa_c = sigma * sqrt(2) * Phi^{-1}( (1 + D)/2 ).                          (13)

At sigma = 0.1: kappa_c = 0.1 -> D = 0.52; kappa_c = 0.3 -> D = 0.966; kappa_c = 0.6 -> D = 0.99998. The existing 7-point kappa_c grid therefore contains NO weak-signal point — |D| >= 0.52 everywhere except 0. Since only the ratio kappa_c/sigma is identified by any rank method, the sweep MUST be reparametrized on D via (13); see experiment_plan.

```python
# sdtemper.py  —  numpy/scipy, drop-in against the existing TracePool harness.
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import rankdata, norm, t as tdist

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- score maps
def within_item_scores(c, transform="normal"):
    """c: (m,) confidences for ONE item -> (m,) scores s."""
    if transform == "raw":  return np.asarray(c, float)                 # CISC-softmax anchor
    if transform == "log":  return np.log(np.clip(c, 1e-6, None))       # CISC-power anchor
    r = rankdata(c, method="average")                                   # midranks, ties handled
    u = (r - 0.375) / (len(c) + 0.25)                                   # Blom plotting positions
    v = norm.ppf(u) if transform == "normal" else (u - 0.5)             # normal | uniform scores
    sd = v.std()
    return np.zeros_like(v) if sd < 1e-12 else (v - v.mean()) / sd      # all-ties -> SC on this item

# ------------------------------------------------- per-item discrimination
def item_auc(c, y):
    """Mann-Whitney U via rank-sum. y in {0,1}. Returns (U, n_pos*n_neg) or None."""
    y = np.asarray(y, bool); npos = int(y.sum()); nneg = len(y) - npos
    if npos == 0 or nneg == 0: return None                              # non-informative item
    r = rankdata(c, method="average")
    U = (r[y].sum() - npos*(npos+1)/2.0) / (npos*nneg)
    return U, float(npos*nneg)

def soft_item_auc(c, t):
    """Weighted Mann-Whitney with soft correctness t in [0,1]. O(m log m) via prefix sums."""
    o = np.argsort(c, kind="mergesort"); cs, ts = np.asarray(c)[o], np.asarray(t)[o]
    num = 0.0
    cum_neg = 0.0                       # sum of (1-t) strictly below current tie group
    i = 0
    while i < len(cs):
        j = i
        while j+1 < len(cs) and cs[j+1] == cs[i]: j += 1
        grp = slice(i, j+1)
        tp, tn = ts[grp].sum(), (1-ts[grp]).sum()
        num += tp*cum_neg + 0.5*tp*tn   # strictly-greater + half the ties
        cum_neg += tn; i = j+1
    den = ts.sum()*(1-ts).sum()
    return (num/den, den) if den > 1e-12 else None

# ---------------------------------------------------- pooling + shrinkage
def pooled_D(items):                    # items: list of (U_q, omega_q)
    U = np.array([u for u, _ in items]); w = np.array([o for _, o in items])
    d = 2*U - 1
    D = float((w*d).sum() / w.sum())
    Qe = len(d)
    var = (Qe/(Qe-1.0)) * ((w**2)*(d-D)**2).sum() / (w.sum()**2)        # cluster sandwich
    return D, float(var), d, w, Qe

def _boot_lambda(d, w, alpha, B=2000, rng=None):                        # item-level BCa half-width (zeta scale)
    rng = rng or np.random.default_rng(0); Q = len(d)
    D0 = (w*d).sum()/w.sum(); z0h = np.arctanh(np.clip(D0, -1+1e-9, 1-1e-9))
    idx = rng.integers(0, Q, size=(B, Q))
    Db = (w[idx]*d[idx]).sum(1) / w[idx].sum(1)
    zb = np.arctanh(np.clip(Db, -1+1e-9, 1-1e-9))
    z0 = norm.ppf(np.clip((zb < z0h).mean(), 1e-6, 1-1e-6))             # bias correction
    jk = np.array([( (np.delete(w,q)*np.delete(d,q)).sum()/np.delete(w,q).sum() ) for q in range(Q)])
    jk = np.arctanh(np.clip(jk, -1+1e-9, 1-1e-9)); jm = jk.mean()
    a = ((jm-jk)**3).sum() / (6.0*(((jm-jk)**2).sum()**1.5) + 1e-12)    # acceleration
    def endpoint(p):
        zp = norm.ppf(p); adj = norm.cdf(z0 + (z0+zp)/(1 - a*(z0+zp)))
        return np.quantile(zb, np.clip(adj, 1e-6, 1-1e-6))
    lo, hi = endpoint(alpha), endpoint(1-alpha)
    return max(z0h - lo, hi - z0h)                                      # conservative half-width

def signed_trust(items, alpha=0.05, boot_max_Q=200, rng=None):
    """-> (rho_hat, D_hat, lambda, Q_eff): CI-lower-bound trust, continuous & odd."""
    D, var, d, w, Qe = pooled_D(items)
    zeta = np.arctanh(np.clip(D, -1+1e-6, 1-1e-6))
    if Qe <= boot_max_Q:
        lam = _boot_lambda(d, w, alpha, rng=rng)
    else:
        se_z = np.sqrt(var) / max(1 - D**2, 1e-9)
        lam = tdist.ppf(1-alpha, Qe-1) * se_z
    rho = np.tanh(np.sign(zeta) * max(0.0, abs(zeta) - lam))            # soft threshold  (eq. 6)
    return float(rho), float(D), float(lam), Qe

# ---------------------------------------------------------- tempering map
def gamma_from_rho(rho, p_bar, gamma_max=4.0, variance_correction=True):
    kap = np.sqrt(2.0) * norm.ppf((1 + np.clip(rho, -1+1e-9, 1-1e-9)) / 2.0)   # eq. 8
    g = kap*np.sqrt(1 + p_bar*(1-p_bar)*kap**2) if variance_correction else kap  # eq. 9
    return float(np.clip(g, -gamma_max, gamma_max))                              # eq. 10

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- vote
def predict_item(c, cluster_id, gamma, K, transform="normal"):
    s = within_item_scores(c, transform)
    z = gamma*s; w = np.exp(z - z.max())                                # overflow-safe, argmax-invariant
    tot = np.bincount(cluster_id, weights=w, minlength=K)
    cnt = np.bincount(cluster_id, minlength=K)
    best = np.max(tot); cand = np.flatnonzero(tot >= best - 1e-12)      # deterministic tie-break
    return cand[np.lexsort((cand, -cnt[cand]))[0]]

# ============================================================ VARIANT (a)
def fit_dev(dev, transform="normal", alpha=0.05, Q_min=20, gamma_max=4.0, seed=0):
    """dev: iterable of items with .c, .cluster_id, .gold_cluster."""
    items, n_tot, n_cor = [], 0, 0
    for it in dev:
        y = (it.cluster_id == it.gold_cluster)
        n_tot += len(y); n_cor += int(y.sum())
        r = item_auc(it.c, y)
        if r is not None: items.append(r)                               # omega_q = n+ * n-
    if len(items) < Q_min:
        return dict(gamma=0.0, D=np.nan, rho=0.0, Q_eff=len(items), reason="insufficient_dev")
    rho, D, lam, Qe = signed_trust(items, alpha, rng=np.random.default_rng(seed))
    p_bar = n_cor / max(n_tot, 1)
    return dict(gamma=gamma_from_rho(rho, p_bar, gamma_max), D=D, rho=rho,
                lam=lam, Q_eff=Qe, p_bar=p_bar)

# ============================================================ VARIANT (b)
def fit_labelfree(pool, transform="normal", alpha=0.05, pi_min=0.5, dup_min=0.5,
                  delta_dup=0.15, phi_max=0.3, em_iters=20, trust_region=1.0,
                  use_em=True, sign_override=None, gamma_max=4.0, seed=0):
    S, CL, PI, AH, K, keep = [], [], [], [], [], []
    for it in pool:
        s = within_item_scores(it.c, transform); k = int(it.cluster_id.max())+1
        cnt = np.bincount(it.cluster_id, minlength=k)
        ah = int(cnt.argmax()); pi = cnt[ah]/len(it.cluster_id)
        ok = pi >= pi_min
        if getattr(it, "sim", None) is not None:                        # M3 echo diagnostic
            n_eff = len(it.c)**2 / it.sim.sum()
            intra = it.sim[np.ix_(it.cluster_id==ah, it.cluster_id==ah)].mean()
            cross = it.sim[np.ix_(it.cluster_id==ah, it.cluster_id!=ah)].mean() if (it.cluster_id!=ah).any() else intra
            ok &= (n_eff/len(it.c) >= dup_min) and (intra - cross <= delta_dup)
        S.append(s); CL.append(it.cluster_id); PI.append(pi); AH.append(ah); K.append(k); keep.append(ok)
    keep = np.array(keep); flagged = 1.0 - keep.mean()
    idx = np.flatnonzero(keep)
    if len(idx) < 20: return dict(gamma=0.0, reason="insufficient_items", flagged=flagged)

    # ---- stage 1: margin-weighted agreement-proxy moment estimator (= EM's 1st iteration)
    items = []
    for q in idx:
        y = (CL[q] == AH[q]); r = item_auc(pool[q].c, y)
        if r is None: continue
        items.append((r[0], r[1]*max(0.0, 2*PI[q]-1)))                  # M1 margin weight
    rho, D0, lam, Qe = signed_trust(items, alpha, rng=np.random.default_rng(seed))
    p_bar = float(np.mean([PI[q] for q in idx]))
    gamma0 = gamma_from_rho(rho, p_bar, gamma_max)
    gamma, beta0 = gamma0, float(np.log(p_bar/(1-p_bar+1e-9)))

    # ---- stage 2: Raykar-style latent-truth EM (soft labels), damped
    if use_em:
        for _ in range(em_iters):
            soft = []
            tot_t, tot_n = 0.0, 0
            for q in idx:
                cs = np.bincount(CL[q], weights=gamma*S[q], minlength=K[q])
                nc = np.bincount(CL[q], minlength=K[q])
                lg = beta0*nc + cs; lg -= lg.max()
                post = np.exp(lg); post /= post.sum()                   # E-step
                tq = post[CL[q]]
                tot_t += tq.sum(); tot_n += len(tq)
                r = soft_item_auc(pool[q].c, tq)
                if r is not None: soft.append((r[0], r[1]*max(0.0, 2*PI[q]-1)))
            if len(soft) < 20: break
            rho_s, D_s, lam_s, _ = signed_trust(soft, alpha, rng=np.random.default_rng(seed))
            p_bar = tot_t/max(tot_n, 1)
            g_raw = gamma_from_rho(rho_s, p_bar, gamma_max)
            g_new = float(np.clip(g_raw, gamma0-trust_region, gamma0+trust_region))  # M-step + trust region
            kap = np.sqrt(2)*norm.ppf((1+np.clip(rho_s,-1+1e-9,1-1e-9))/2)
            beta0 = float(np.log(p_bar/(1-p_bar+1e-9)) + kap**2*(2*p_bar-1)/2)
            if abs(g_new - gamma) < 1e-3: gamma = g_new; break
            gamma = g_new
    if flagged > phi_max: gamma *= (1.0 - flagged)                      # M3 global damping
    if sign_override is not None: gamma = abs(gamma)*np.sign(sign_override)   # M4 dev sign certification
    return dict(gamma=float(gamma), D_proxy=D0, rho=rho, flagged=flagged, Q_eff=Qe)

# ------------------------------------------------------------ online loop
def run_online(stream, burn_in=50, refresh=25, window=400, **kw):
    hist, gamma, preds = [], 0.0, []
    for n, it in enumerate(stream):
        preds.append(predict_item(it.c, it.cluster_id, gamma,
                                  int(it.cluster_id.max())+1, kw.get("transform","normal")))
        hist.append(it)                                                 # M5: item q never informs its own gamma
        if len(hist) >= burn_in and (len(hist)-burn_in) % refresh == 0:
            gamma = fit_labelfree(hist[-window:], **kw)["gamma"]
    return preds
```

## A. Setup
Prediction rule: a_hat_q(gamma, psi) = argmax_a S_q(a) with S_q(a) = sum_{i : cl(a_{qi}) = a} exp(gamma * psi(c_q)_i), tie-broken by the fixed deterministic rule (max n_{qa}, then min cluster id). "Reduces exactly" below means the two rules induce IDENTICAL predictions on every item of every pool, including ties — not merely equal in a limit.

## B. Zero trust => plain SC, EXACTLY
Set gamma = 0. Then for every i, w_{qi} = exp(0 * s_{qi}) = e^0 = 1 regardless of psi and regardless of c. Hence
    S_q(a) = sum_{i : cl(a_{qi}) = a} 1 = n_{qa},
which is the SC vote count function verbatim; the argmax and the tie-break (which is itself defined on n_{qa}) coincide. So a_hat_q(0, psi) = a_hat_q^{SC} for all q, all psi, all pools. QED.

Two further exactness facts, both stronger than a limit statement:
(B1) gamma_hat = 0 is ATTAINED on a positive-measure event, not approached asymptotically. By (6), rho_hat = tanh(S_lambda(atanh D_hat)) = 0 iff |atanh D_hat| <= lambda, i.e. iff the (1-2*alpha) confidence interval for D covers 0; and g(0; p_bar) = sqrt(2)*Phi^{-1}(1/2) * sqrt(1+0) = 0, so gamma_hat = clip(0) = 0. Therefore SD-Temper IS plain SC — same code path, same outputs — whenever the dev evidence for a signed association is not significant. Consequence: P(gamma_hat != 0 | true D = 0) <= 2*alpha = 0.10 at the default alpha = 0.05.
(B2) Per-item SC fallback: if all confidences within item q are tied, sd(v) = 0 and psi_rank returns s == 0, so w = exp(0) = 1 and item q is decided by SC for ANY gamma. Lumpy/ceiling verbalized confidence therefore degrades to SC item-by-item, automatically.

## C. Full trust => CISC, EXACTLY (bit-for-bit, both published forms)
CISC's published rule is the within-question softmax-normalized weighted vote
    a_hat_q^{CISC}(T) = argmax_a sum_{i : cl(a_{qi}) = a} [ exp(c_{qi}/T) / Z_q ],   Z_q = sum_{j=1}^{m_q} exp(c_{qj}/T).
Normalization-irrelevance lemma: Z_q > 0 does not depend on a, so for all a, S_q^{CISC,norm}(a) = S_q^{CISC,unnorm}(a)/Z_q, a strictly positive common rescaling; argmax and every order relation among candidate scores are preserved, and the tie set is preserved exactly. Hence
    a_hat_q^{CISC}(T) = argmax_a sum_{i in a} exp(c_{qi}/T).
Now instantiate SD-Temper with psi = psi_raw (psi(c)_i = c_i) and gamma = 1/T:
    S_q(a) = sum_{i in a} exp( (1/T) * c_{qi} ) = sum_{i in a} exp(c_{qi}/T).
The two score functions are the same function of the same data, so the predictions are identical for every item, every pool, and every tie configuration. Therefore SD-Temper(psi_raw, gamma = 1/T) IS CISC(T). QED.
(The implementation makes this literal: `predict_item` computes exp(gamma*s - max(gamma*s)), which differs from exp(gamma*s) by the positive common factor exp(-max), again argmax-preserving.)

Power-form CISC (the seed's w_i = c_i^gamma): take psi = psi_log, psi(c)_i = log c_i (c_i >= 0.01 by the simulator's clip, so the log is finite). Then exp(gamma * log c_i) = c_i^gamma identically, so SD-Temper(psi_log, gamma) IS power-CISC(gamma). QED.

Rank mode's own full-trust anchor: with psi_rank, the corresponding full-trust member is rank-CISC (published as self-certainty Borda voting with exponent p, up to the monotone reparametrization of the rank scale). Moreover the gamma -> +inf limit recovers CISC's T -> 0 anchor: if the maximizing score s_(m) is unique, then
    S_q(a) / exp(gamma * s_(m)) = 1[a = cl(a_{q,(m)})] + sum_{i in a, i != (m)} exp(gamma (s_i - s_(m))) -> 1[a = cl(a_{q,(m)})]
as gamma -> +inf, since every exponent s_i - s_(m) < 0. So a_hat_q -> the answer of the single highest-confidence trace = argmax-confidence = lim_{T->0} CISC(T). Symmetrically gamma -> -inf gives argmin-confidence, which is the correct behaviour for a perfectly anti-correlated channel and is unreachable by CISC (whose softmax weight is monotone increasing in c for every T > 0). This asymmetry is precisely the R5 gap.

## D. Continuity, oddness, monotonicity of the tempering map
Let kappa(rho) = sqrt(2) * Phi^{-1}((1+rho)/2) on rho in (-1,1).
 (D1) kappa is continuous and strictly increasing (composition of the strictly increasing continuous Phi^{-1} with an increasing affine map).
 (D2) kappa(0) = sqrt(2) Phi^{-1}(1/2) = 0.
 (D3) kappa is ODD: Phi^{-1}(1-u) = -Phi^{-1}(u) by symmetry of the standard normal, and (1+(-rho))/2 = 1 - (1+rho)/2, so kappa(-rho) = -kappa(rho).
 (D4) h(x) = x*sqrt(1 + c x^2) with c = p_bar(1-p_bar) in [0, 1/4] is odd, continuous, and strictly increasing: h'(x) = sqrt(1+cx^2) + c x^2 / sqrt(1+c x^2) > 0 for all x.
 Hence g = h o kappa is continuous, odd, strictly increasing, with g(0) = 0, g(rho) -> +inf as rho -> 1^-, g(rho) -> -inf as rho -> -1^+. Clipping to [-gamma_max, gamma_max] preserves continuity and (weak) monotonicity and preserves oddness (clip is odd). With gamma_max = 4 and p_bar = 1/2 the cap binds only for |rho| > 0.995 (kappa = 4/sqrt(1+kappa^2/4) => kappa ~ 2.83, rho = 2*Phi(2.0)-1 = 0.9545 for the uncorrected map; 0.995 with correction) — i.e. only where the vote is effectively argmax-confidence anyway.

## E. Continuity, oddness, monotonicity of the shrinkage operator
S_lambda(x) = sign(x) max(0, |x| - lambda) is continuous in (x, lambda) (it is 1-Lipschitz in x), odd in x, non-decreasing in x, non-increasing in lambda; tanh and atanh are continuous, odd, strictly increasing bijections between (-1,1) and R. Therefore rho_hat = tanh(S_lambda(atanh D_hat)) is:
 (E1) continuous in (D_hat, lambda) — no jumps anywhere, in particular none at the trust/no-trust boundary, which is what a hard gate has and what G2 forbids;
 (E2) odd in D_hat: rho_hat(-D_hat) = -rho_hat(D_hat) — negative discrimination is exploited symmetrically, not merely tolerated;
 (E3) non-decreasing in D_hat, non-increasing in lambda (more estimator uncertainty => strictly less trust);
 (E4) |rho_hat| <= |D_hat| with equality only when lambda = 0 — the estimator never trusts MORE than the point estimate;
 (E5) zero set {D_hat : |atanh D_hat| <= lambda} is a closed interval around 0 whose width grows monotonically with SE.
Composing, gamma_hat = clip(g(rho_hat)) is a continuous, odd, monotone function of the data through the single sufficient pair (D_hat, SE), and it depends on the raw confidences only through their within-item ranks when psi = psi_rank (so any strictly monotone recalibration of the channel leaves gamma_hat AND the predictions numerically unchanged — the monotone-invariance claim, testable exactly by regime G-MONO).

## F. The two limits of the trust dial, in SNR terms
Write SNR = |atanh D_hat| / SE_zeta.
 (F1) SNR -> 0 (uninformative or unmeasurable channel, e.g. Q_eff small, ties, D = 0): lambda >= SNR * SE_zeta => S_lambda(atanh D_hat) = 0 => rho_hat = 0 => gamma_hat = 0 => the algorithm is plain SC by B. 
 (F2) SE_zeta -> 0 with D_hat -> 1 (large dev, perfectly discriminative channel): lambda -> 0, rho_hat -> D_hat -> 1, gamma_hat -> gamma_max, and by C the rule -> argmax-confidence = CISC at T -> 0. For intermediate D_hat with SE -> 0, gamma_hat -> g(D_hat), an interior CISC-family member.
So SD-Temper traverses the SC <-> CISC segment continuously and monotonically in the estimated signal-to-noise ratio of the channel's signed discrimination, hitting both endpoints exactly.

## G. Bounded-perturbation (decision-agreement) lemma — the formal backbone of "never significantly below SC"
Let S_m = max_i |s_{qi}| (for psi_rank with m = 40, S_m ~ 2.3; in general S_m <= Phi^{-1}(1 - 3/(8m+2))/sd(v)). For any gamma,
    n_{qa} e^{-|gamma| S_m} <= S_q(a) <= n_{qa} e^{+|gamma| S_m}.
Hence if a is the SC winner and b any rival with n_{qa}/n_{qb} > e^{2 |gamma| S_m}, then S_q(a) >= n_{qa} e^{-|gamma|S_m} > n_{qb} e^{+|gamma|S_m} >= S_q(b), so SD-Temper also prefers a. Therefore:
    { q : a_hat_q(gamma) != a_hat_q^{SC} } is contained in { q : n_(1),q / n_(2),q <= exp(2 |gamma_hat| S_m) },
where n_(1), n_(2) are the top-two SC counts. As gamma_hat -> 0 this containing set shrinks to the SC ties, so the disagreement measure -> 0 continuously; the maximum achievable accuracy loss versus SC is bounded by the mass of low-margin items times their SC accuracy. This is a worst-case guard and is loose at moderate gamma (at gamma = 0.3, S_m = 2.3, the bound only certifies items with count ratio > 4.0), but it is non-vacuous and it is the exact sense in which trust magnitude controls deviation from SC.

## H. What is NOT proved (state this in the paper; do not overclaim)
 (H1) No dominance/regret theorem. G2 ("never significantly below SC") is an EMPIRICAL claim, supported by (B1) exact-SC attainment, (E) continuity, (G) bounded perturbation, and the alpha-level control P(gamma_hat != 0 | D = 0) <= 2 alpha — not by a proof of no-loss at gamma_hat != 0.
 (H2) The tempering map g is exact only under the rank-normal Gaussian equal-variance model of §4; under tail-only informativeness (regime G-TAIL) the LLR is not linear in s and g mis-scales the MAGNITUDE of gamma_hat. The SIGN and the SC/CISC anchors are unaffected (they do not use the model), so the failure is graceful.
 (H3) The default aggregator is multiplicative (for the exact CISC anchor) while the Bayes-optimal aggregator under conditional independence is additive in log-odds; they agree only to first order in gamma. Ablation A9 (LOGPOOL) measures the gap.
 (H4) For the LABEL-FREE variant the sign of D is NOT identifiable: by (11), the observable D^{agr} = (1-eps)D + eps E is invariant under the pair-swap (D<0, eps=0) <-> (D>0, eps=1, E=D), i.e. "competent plurality + anti-correlated confidence" and "echo plurality + correlated confidence" are observationally equivalent. This is the Parisi et al. (PNAS 2014) global sign ambiguity in a two-view (agreement x confidence) disguise, and no amount of unlabeled data resolves it. Hence G2 for SD-Temper-LF is stated CONDITIONALLY on a plurality-competence assumption (eps < eps* = |D|/(|D|+E)), or the sign bit is taken from a >= 25-item labeled set (M4). This is a theorem of impossibility, presented as a limitation, not a bug.

## E5. Statistics (pre-registered, correction-explicit)
Per cell, with N paired items, b = #(A right, B wrong), c = #(A wrong, B right):
  Delta_hat = (b - c)/N,  SE(Delta_hat) = sqrt( (b + c) - (b - c)^2/N ) / N.
  Superiority: exact McNemar binomial on (b, c). Non-inferiority at margin delta: reject "A worse than B by >= delta" iff Delta_hat - z_{0.95} * SE > -delta.
Multiplicity: Holm-Bonferroni across the full pre-registered family of cells for each falsifier, at family-wise alpha = 0.05. Power: at N = 8000 with discordance rate ~0.08, the minimum detectable |Delta| is ~0.007 at 80% power -- this is what fixes the non-inferiority margins below at 0.005 (slightly under the detection floor, i.e. deliberately strict).
Also report, per method: (i) the frontier-area score = mean accuracy over the 13-point D grid at matched budget; (ii) the WORST-CELL score = min accuracy over all (regime, D, m) cells; (iii) regret-to-ORACLE.

PNAS 2014 sign ambiguity in two-view disguise). Sign flips once eps > |D|/(|D|+E) -- e.g. eps* = 0.385 at D=-0.5, E=+0.8. HETEROGENEOUS PER-ITEM DISCRIMINATION BREAKS THE SINGLE-GLOBAL-GAMMA MODEL. Under D_q ~ TruncNormal(0.4, 0.45) a scalar reliability functional is misspecified: the estimator returns a variance-weighted average of per-item D_q, which is optimal for none of them. A GLAD-style per-item gamma is data-starved at m=40 (<= ~400 within-item pairs, and only ~n+ n- of them informative). Scope the claim explicitly to CHANNEL-level tempering and report the oracle per-item envelope as the disclosed gap.

SMALL BUDGETS STARVE THE FUNCTIONAL. At m = 4 an informative item contributes at most 4 (typically 1-3) within-item pairs; sd_q(d_hat_q) is huge, lambda is large, gamma_hat is shrunk toward 0, and SD-Temper loses to CISC on friendly regimes (D >= 0.7). This is the most likely locus of an F1 failure. Partial remedy: pool across items on a common calibration scale (fit a single logistic p(correct|s) rather than per-item ranks) at m <= 8, at the cost of monotone invariance -- ship as an option, not the default.

TIE-HEAVY / CEILING CONFIDENCE COLLAPSES THE RANK SCORE. Real verbalized confidences pile on {0.9, 0.95, 0.99}; midranks make s nearly constant, sd(v) -> 0, and the method degrades to SC. This is SAFE (never below SC) but yields no gain, and it also depresses D_hat so the estimator correctly reports 'no usable channel'. Symptom to monitor: within-item sd of s and the fraction of all-tie items.

ESTIMATOR JITTER NEAR D = 0 (the F2 risk). With shrink_rule='none' the point estimate oscillates around 0 and gamma_hat flips sign across seeds, which can drop accuracy below SC at |D| <= 0.10. The soft-threshold/LCB rule is what prevents this; ablation A2 is expected to demonstrate the failure. Related: if the CI is computed with pooled-pairs DeLong instead of item-clustered resampling, SE is understated by roughly sqrt(m) and the same failure returns (ablation A11).

THE GAUSSIAN-LLR TEMPERING MAP IS MISSPECIFIED WHEN CONFIDENCE IS INFORMATIVE ONLY IN THE TAILS (G-TAIL). The true log-likelihood ratio is then non-linear in s, so g() mis-scales the MAGNITUDE of gamma_hat (typically under-trusting, because the pooled AUC averages an uninformative middle with informative tails). Sign and the SC/CISC anchors are unaffected, so the failure is graceful, not catastrophic. A monotone-spline LLR fit on dev is the natural extension and is deliberately out of scope.

MULTIPLICATIVE vs ADDITIVE AGGREGATION MISMATCH. The default w = exp(gamma*s) form is chosen for the exact CISC anchor, but the Bayes-optimal aggregator under conditional independence is additive in log-odds; the two agree only to first order in gamma. At large |gamma_hat| the multiplicative form over-weights a single extreme trace relative to the Bayes rule. Ablation A9 (LOGPOOL) measures the gap; expect it to matter only at |gamma| > 2.

DEV -> TEST DISTRIBUTION SHIFT DEFEATS THE DEV VARIANT (by construction). In G-SHIFT (dev at D=+0.7, test at D=-0.3), SD-Temper-Dev applies a confidently wrong-signed gamma and should perform like CISC, i.e. badly. This is not a bug to hide: it is the pre-registered justification for the label-free/online variant, and it is the ONLY axis on which SD-Temper-Dev can beat CISC's published dev-tuned-T protocol (they are near-twins on iid splits).

CONDITIONAL ESTIMAND. D is estimated only on items having both a correct and an incorrect trace. When accuracy is near 0 or 1 the informative-item pool shrinks (Q_eff << n_dev) and D estimates discrimination conditional on a non-representative subpopulation. Q_min guards the degenerate case by falling back to SC, but the conditioning bias itself is unaddressed -- report Q_eff/n_dev in every results table.

F4 IS GENUINELY LIKELY TO FIRE ON THE FRIENDLY HALF OF THE SWEEP. Weighted-vote accuracy is famously flat in gamma over wide ranges; for D >= 0.4 almost any positive gamma wins, so CISC's dev-tuned T, a binary WQD gate, and SD-Temper will be indistinguishable. The claim must therefore be staked on the WORST-CELL metric and the D < 0 half, not on average accuracy. If the sign-corrected 3-way gate {-1,0,+1} also matches SD-Temper everywhere, continuous tempering is refuted and the paper must be published as that negative result.

EM SELF-CONFIRMATION. The Raykar EM's E-step uses the current gamma to build soft labels, which then re-estimate gamma; in echo regimes this is a positive feedback loop that drives gamma toward strongly trusting the echo cluster. The trust region (Delta_max = 1.0), the per-M-step shrinkage, and the iteration cap are the brakes; monitor the gamma trajectory across iterations and abort on monotone divergence.

MULTIPLE-COMPARISON FRAGILITY OF G2 AS STATED. 'Never significantly below SC anywhere' over ~95 cells is either trivially true (with correction) or trivially false (without it). The claim is only meaningful with the pre-registered non-inferiority margin (delta2 = 0.005), the Holm correction at FWER 0.05, and the declared per-family cell list fixed BEFORE running -- and even then it is an empirical claim, not a theorem (anchor proof H1).
